input: A dispatch office employs 12 full-time staff. Overtime was 16% of paid hours last year. The recommendation is to replace half the overtime with one additional hire, at $87k per year fully loaded, with the staffing decision held by the office's management. Overtime is concentrated in two seasonal peaks. A hire is paid for the full year, including the months outside the peaks, and the $87k cost stands on that basis. The comparison is therefore between overtime paid at peak periods only and a salary paid across the whole year. Half the overtime is replaced, not all of it: cover at the peaks still draws on overtime after the hire, and the remaining overtime stays available for the weeks when demand exceeds the pattern of the previous year. The case for the hire rests on the share of hours involved. At 16% of paid hours, overtime is a standing feature of the office's staffing, not an occasional supplement, and a standing share of that size is the part of the pattern a permanent post can carry. The office also gains cover independent of existing staff working additional hours at the peaks, where an overtime pattern is most exposed. The retained overtime still depends on such willingness, so the exposure is reduced, not removed.
